title: Orbits and escape: Newton's cannon
objective: Learners launch a body from 300 km above an Earth-like planet and see that speed, not height, decides its fate: below circular speed it falls back, at circular speed it circles, between circular and escape speed it traces an ellipse whose far side rises with every extra metre per second, and at escape speed it never returns. The closed-form orbit predicts the shape; the integrated path confirms it.

recommended.why: A top-down view with the planet, the growing trajectory and the moving body is the picture everyone remembers from Newton's cannon; p5 draws it in real time from the model's path.

alternative.why: The flat view shows the shape; the 3D view shows the orbit as a path around a globe you can turn. Does depth add anything for an orbit that lies in a plane?

assumptions: Two-body motion around a point mass; no atmosphere, no rotation, no other bodies; an Earth-like planet (radius 6,371 km, μ = 398,600 km³/s² scaled by the mass control)
Launch from 300 km altitude at the chosen speed and angle above horizontal; gravity is the only force afterwards

The closed-form orbit (specific energy, angular momentum, semi-major axis, eccentricity, periapsis and apoapsis, period) is computed at launch; the path is integrated with RK4 at 720 samples over up to two periods (or four hours for an escape) and stops at impact
Playback compresses the simulated span into 24 s, so one second on screen is minutes of flight
Distances in km, speeds in km/s, time in minutes and hours
units: distance: km; time: minutes and hours
checkDescription: Energy is conserved along the integrated path within 0.5 %; its lowest and highest points match the closed-form periapsis and apoapsis within 1 %; the outcome follows the energy sign and the periapsis; the path ends on the surface exactly when it crashes; the time between periapsis passes matches Kepler's period within 2 % when two passes fit the window; escape speed is √2 × circular speed.

learnerPrompts.predict: Set the speed to 7.5 km/s (just under circular) before you play. Where will the body be lowest: above the launch point, or on the far side of the planet?
learnerPrompts.explain: At 11 km/s the body escapes Earth but not a planet of twice the mass. Explain why the same speed gives different fates, using the energy number the lesson shows.
